notes_endorse: Editorial 'Two Good Republicans': 'we would not blame a great many of the voters for putting their support behind Jonas and Stevens. They are good men.' Jonas described as 'a strong incumbent.'
Editorial 'Two Good Republicans': running against young Congressman Hugh Alexander, supports him as 'a good man.'
Editorial argues Gavin would face 'serious trouble handling chief executive's duties with divided leadership' and is 'only a moderately able G.O.P. chief executive.'

Editorial 'The Overriding Issue: Divided Government': While critical of Moore's bland campaign, paper argues against divided government - 'the people of North Carolina should seriously consider whether the two-party system should be strengthened at the grass roots before projecting only a moderately able G.O.P. chief executive into the Governor's Mansion.' Effectively endorses Moore.
Editorial 'Johnson Or Goldwater: Unity Or Division?' framing of editorial title suggests Johnson endorsement (Goldwater seen as divisive); image too small to read in full detail.
Editorial recommends 'attorney general, Robert Morgan'
Editorial 'For statewide offices': recommends 'state auditor, Henry Bridges'
Editorial recommends 'commissioner of agriculture, James A. Graham'
Editorial recommends 'commissioner of labor, Frank Crane'
Editorial endorses Scott over Gardner; Gardner described as inexperienced and lacking judgment.
Editorial 'Bob Scott — an easy choice' endorses Bob Scott (D) for NC Governor over Republican Jim Gardner.
Editorial endorses Preyer over Osteen. Notes Osteen's party 'is by all signs unlikely to regain control of the House this year.'
Editorial 'Preyer for Congress': 'we believe L. Richardson Preyer to be that man' (more capable for 6th District).
Editorial recommends 'insurance commissioner, Edwin S. Lanier'
Editorial: incumbent Superior Court judge in 22nd district being challenged; editorial backs incumbents on principle.
Editorial: 'Judge Ervin was recently appointed to the bench by Governor Moore'; backs incumbents.
Editorial: 'His opponent Don H. Garren is a young Republican legislator of limited experience.'
Editorial: 'H. Pat Taylor Jr., the Democratic nominee, is a former speaker of the House and a man of seasoned judgment.'

Editorial 'The '68 presidential choice' discusses Wallace ('The third party'), Nixon ('An authentic conservative'), and Humphrey ('The transparent Mr. Humphrey'). Headline structure and section labels favor Nixon. Image too small to confirm endorsement language with full confidence.

Editorial 'For statewide offices': 'Sen. Sam J. Ervin Jr. — despite our more than occasional disagreements with him — holds an edge of experience, senatorial seniority and personal ability that it would be foolish to cast away in a vote for his all too obscure opponent, Robert V. Somers.'
Described as 'all too obscure opponent' to Ervin.
Editorial recommends 'state superintendent of public instruction, Craig Phillips'
Editorial recommends 'state treasurer, Edwin Gill'
Editorial 'Two for Congress' endorses incumbent congressman Preyer (D) in 6th District based on prior endorsements; image too small for full text confirmation.
Editorial 'The legislative race' endorses Hargrove Bowles Jr. and Edwin Edwards for state senate.
Editorial endorses Hargrove Bowles Jr. and Edwin Edwards for state senate.

Editorial 'A selection for governor' on 1972 NC governor's race (Bowles D vs Holshouser R). Image too small to read with certainty; based on paper's typical lean and editorial reasoning visible suggests Bowles endorsement.
Editorial 'We like Ike' likely refers to Ike Andrews, Democratic candidate for 4th NC Congressional District in 1972. Image too small to confirm.
Editorial 'Clark in the Eighth' endorses Clark for 8th NC Congressional District seat. (Likely refers to Bill Clark, Democratic challenger.) Image too small for full text.
Editorial 'Hunt for lieutenant governor' endorses Jim Hunt (D) for NC Lt Governor in 1972. Headline clear, content not readable in detail.

Editorial 'For attorney general' opposes Carson. James Carson was recently appointed by Governor Holshouser to fill the unexpired term of Robert Morgan as state attorney general. Editorial endorses Edmisten instead.
Editorial 'For attorney general': 'We recommend Mr. Edmisten's election.' Despite Edmisten's lack of executive experience, editorial sees him as more promising candidate over James Carson.

Editorial 'County offices' endorses incumbent Democrat Joseph Shore for Clerk of Guilford Superior Court (CNTY CLERK). Praised as most capable and knowledgeable clerk of Superior Court in NC; in office since 1940.
Republican challenger for Clerk of Guilford Superior Court; not endorsed.

Editorial endorses Democrat Ray Alexander for Solicitor (DA) of 18th Judicial District. Was first legal aid attorney in Greensboro, respected member of local bar; proposes changes in procedure to save taxpayer money and time for jurors/witnesses.
Republican challenger for Solicitor of 18th Judicial District; not endorsed.

Editorial 'Ike in the Fourth District' endorses Ike Andrews (D), described as 'truly outstanding state legislator' who 'will distinguish himself in Washington.' 'we trust that the Fourth District voters... will return Mr. Andrews.'

Editorial: 'Mr. Purrington, a Republican, made a respectable career during his brief stint as the Statehouse. But his performance as a legislator by no means compares.' Editorial recommends voters reject him.

Editorial 'Preyer for Congress' endorses incumbent L. Richardson Preyer (D) for re-election to 6th NC Congressional District. Editorial praises Preyer's reputation, advertising and supporters including President Ford, Henry Kissinger.

Editorial: 'Mr. Morgan has steadily denied — which Mr. Morgan has steadily denied — would demonstrate his superior grasp of the issues facing the country.' Editorial concludes Stevens is the better choice.

Editorial 'Stevens for the Senate': 'we believe that a vote for Mr. Stevens on November 5 is the better of the alternatives facing North Carolina.' Stevens described as a 'genteel GOP moderate of the Holshouser stamp.'

Editorial endorses incumbent Democratic Sheriff Paul Gibson for re-election. Even-handed, professional law enforcement man; eight years in office; capable job despite friction with Republican-controlled County Commissioners.
Republican challenger for Sheriff; not endorsed.
Editorial endorses Sharp over Newsom. Newsom 'has no qualifications at all for the post of Chief Justice. He is not a lawyer.'

Editorial 'Miss Sharp for CJ' endorses Justice Susie Sharp (D) for NC Supreme Court Chief Justice over Robert Newsom of Wilkesboro (R). 'We trust that the voters of North Carolina, regardless of party, will follow their good example.'

Editorial 'For clerk of court: Shore' endorses incumbent Joseph P. Shore (D, age 67) for Clerk of Guilford Superior Court (CNTY CLERK). In office since 1940. Operations efficient, smooth-running. Despite controversy over disturbing the peace plea, deserves another term.
Republican challenger for Clerk of Court; High Point attorney, age 32. Bright and articulate but not endorsed.
Editorial 'Three for the county' endorses incumbent Democrat Gaston Faison for Guilford County Board of Commissioners. Praised for plain-spoken views and creating county alcohol treatment center.
Editorial endorses incumbent Democrat Bert Hall for County Commissioner. Retired county agricultural agent with strong ties to rural and black communities.
Republican candidate for County Commissioner. Editorial calls him an 'impressive' newcomer but does not endorse, preferring greater experience of three endorsed candidates.
Editorial endorses Republican Odell Payne for County Commissioner. Former three-term member of NC House; would bring departure from board's all-Democratic flavor.
Democrat candidate for County Commissioner. Editorial calls him an 'impressive' newcomer but does not endorse, preferring greater experience of three endorsed candidates.
Republican challenger to Judge Erwin; Hickory attorney. Not endorsed.
Editorial 'For appellate, superior court' endorses Richard C. Erwin (D) for NC Court of Appeals. Winston-Salem attorney appointed by Governor Hunt; first black member of court of appeals.

Editorial 'Schlosser for DA' recommends Mike Schlosser (D) for district attorney of the 18th Judicial District (Guilford County). Beat incumbent Ray Alexander in Democratic primary. Endorsement comes with reservations about $6,000 gift episode and judgment, but cites recent and proven track record in prosecuting difficult jury cases.
Republican opponent for DA. Editorial says Stanback would prove competent but his experience as assistant prosecutor was 10 years ago and limited. Not endorsed.
Republican challenger to Preyer; described as feisty, conservative campaign capitalizing on anti-tax mood. Not endorsed.

Editorial 'The Preyer record' endorses incumbent L. Richardson Preyer (D) for re-election to US House 6th District. Praised for thoughtful, independent leadership; chaired ethics code and JFK/MLK assassinations investigations.
Republican challenger; former District Court Judge appointed by former Gov. Jim Holshouser. Not endorsed.

Editorial endorses District Court Judge Edward K. Washington (D) for Superior Court seat in Guilford County's 18th Judicial District. Currently chief judge of Guilford District Court; cited longer experience and reputation for fairness.
Editorial 'For county school board' endorses Francis Delaune, 38, airline agent from Oak Ridge. Ran for school board in 1976 and was narrowly defeated. Nonpartisan race; 4 seats.
Editorial endorses Melvin Griffin, 44, state parole officer. One of two black candidates running for school board. Nonpartisan.
Editorial endorses Mrs. Carolyn H. McGee, 43, housewife from Forest Oaks. Nonpartisan school board race.
Editorial endorses Mrs. Ann Talbert, 36, former elementary school teacher from Oak Ridge. Nonpartisan school board race.

Editorial 'A dismal choice' explicitly declines to endorse incumbent Republican Senator Jesse Helms. 'Senator Helms's abysmal record speaks for itself. His career as a television editorialist, campaigner and senator is a monument to narrow ideology and diehard opposition.' Not endorsed.

Editorial 'A dismal choice' declines to endorse Democratic challenger John Ingram. 'Mr. Ingram's shortcoming is not that he is too liberal, or even too conservative, but that he is too shallow.' Not endorsed.
Editorial 'Gibson for sheriff' endorses incumbent Democrat Paul H. Gibson for Guilford County Sheriff. Seeking fourth term, 33 years of service in the department.
Republican challenger; political newcomer with no law enforcement experience; not qualified per editorial.

Editorial endorses Republican J. Howard Coble for State House. Served a term in House from Guilford ten years ago; former secretary of revenue in Holshouser administration. 'We recommend his election.'
Editorial endorses Republican William T. (Bill) Evans Jr., land developer from Summerfield. 'We like him, and commend his candidacy to the voters.'
Editorial endorses Democrat Tom Foster, assistant county attorney and political newcomer. 'We support his candidacy enthusiastically.'

Editorial '...And the House' endorses incumbent Democrat Henry E. Frye, Greensboro attorney, seeking sixth term. Senior delegation member; chaired one of three judiciary committees; instrumental in passing first landlord-tenant bill.
Editorial endorses Democrat Byron Haworth (incumbent appointed to fill Tom Gilmore's seat). Retired District Court Judge, age 71; long bench experience.
Editorial recommends Republican Margaret P. Keesee for State House. Elected to House in 1974 but lost reelection bid; school teacher; 'would be a conscientious member of the delegation.'
Editorial endorses incumbent Democrat Jim Morgan, High Point attorney. Strong recommended re-election; whirlwind of activity in first term.
Editorial endorses incumbent Democrat Mary Seymour for second term. Eight years on Greensboro City Council.
Republican challenger; local businessman; former city council member; not endorsed.
Republican challenger; local businessman; impressed editorial board with homework on issues but not endorsed.
Editorial endorses incumbent Democrat Rachel Gray for State Senate. Former mayor pro tem of High Point.
Republican challenger; has made few campaign appearances; not endorsed.

Editorial 'For the legislature: The Senate' endorses incumbent Democrat Kathy Sebo for re-election to NC State Senate (Guilford). Chairman of Guilford delegation, seeking third term; college professor enrolled in law school.
Editorial endorses Democrat Jim Turner for State Senate. Greensboro attorney; unseated veteran Democratic lawmaker Mark Short in spring primary.

Editorial 'For commissioner' endorses incumbent Democrat Forrest Campbell for re-election to Guilford County Board of Commissioners. Chairman for last three years; skillfully guided board through difficult times including tax revaluation. 'Strongly recommend his re-election.'
Republican challenger; retired county employee; served a term on board of commissioners in early 1960s. Not endorsed.

Editorial endorses incumbent Democrat Ogden Deal for re-election to County Commissioners. Sculptor from McLeansville. 'Our nod goes to Ogden Deal. He provides balance to the board.' Praised for knowledge of environmental issues.

Republican challenger; businessman from McLeansville area; served three terms in NC House. Editorial says 'we think he would make a good commissioner' but if a choice must be made, endorses Deal. Not endorsed.
Republican challenger to Preyer. Editorial: 'Gene Johnston has run a good race. But his promise is no match for Preyer's performance.' Not endorsed.

Editorial 'Preyer for Congress' endorses incumbent Richardson Preyer (D) for Sixth District US House. Praised for moderate voting record, work on agricultural support programs, tobacco and textile industries, and chairing new code of ethics development. 'Richardson Preyer has served the Sixth District and North Carolina well.'

Two-term Democratic incumbent Insurance Commissioner. Editorial calls for him to be voted out, citing abuse of office, clashes with industry, questionable travel expenses, and high-handed regulation style.

Editorial 'Vote out Ingram' endorses Republican Ed Tenney for NC Insurance Commissioner. Native of Chapel Hill, real estate agent who owned/operated insurance agency for six years. Ran unsuccessfully against Ingram in 1976. 'We recommend him for the job.'

Editorial 'For District Court' endorses Democrat E.L. Alston Jr. for District Court Judge to replace retiring Judge John Hatfield. Veteran Greensboro defense attorney with nearly 30 years of courtroom experience.
Republican opponent for District Court Judge; able young Greensboro lawyer; lacks Alston's experience. Not endorsed.

Editorial 'strongly recommends' Democrat William 'Pete' Hunter for second District Court vacancy. Age 37; former teacher/coach in High Point schools; assistant DA and now on Guilford County Public Defender's staff.
Republican opponent of High Point, age 49; ran for judgeship in 1976 and lost. Editorial criticizes him for racist campaign flyer. Not endorsed.

Editorial 'For President' endorses incumbent President Jimmy Carter (D) for re-election. 'We think President Carter's superior knowledge and experience justify his re-election.' Praised for SALT II treaty, energy program, environmental record, foreign policy restraint, and judicial/regulatory appointments.
Republican challenger Ronald Reagan; editorial criticizes his arms build-up plans, Kemp-Roth tax cut as inflationary, dismantling of Department of Energy, brinksmanship foreign policy. Not endorsed.

Editorial 'For Register of Deeds' endorses Republican Kay Patseavouras of High Point. 'Lacks specific experience, but would learn quickly. She is energetic and clearly works well with people. We recommend her for the job.'

Four-term Democratic incumbent Register of Deeds, age 68. Editorial argues for change citing pattern of indifference, land transactions controversy, and elections board fine for promotional package distribution. Not endorsed.

Editorial 'The county school fuss' defends incumbent chairman Evon Dean (Guilford County Board of Education) against last-minute campaign attacks; says 'have worked hard for the schools and...have done a good job of presiding over enormous change in four years' time.' Effectively endorses incumbent.
Editorial commends third incumbent William K. Gragg, recently appointed to the board, who 'has also given capable, if quiet, service.' Effectively endorses.
Editorial defends incumbent Nancy Jo Smith against last-minute campaign attacks; commends her work for the schools. Effectively endorses incumbent.
District 1 opponent; former Greensboro Redevelopment Commission engineer. Not endorsed.
Editorial endorses James T. Williams Jr. (attorney) for school board District 1 (northern). 'Among the best-prepared of all candidates for the job.' Former president of Cone PTA.
Editorial endorses Robert L. Meadows Jr. for school board District 2. Works for US Postal Service; on board of directors of Youth Care; on principal selection study committee.
District 2 opponent; advertising salesman for WGBG; head of North O. Henry Oaks Community Association; opposed school districting. Not endorsed.
District 3 opponent; ran active campaign. Not endorsed.
Editorial endorses Pershing E. Wall Sr. for school board District 3 (southeast). US Mail Service supervisor; treasurer of NC Congress of Parents and Teachers.
Editorial endorses incumbent Jo Ann Scoggin for school board District 4 (southwest). Children in schools for 20+ years; worked hard on school redistricting.
District 5 opponent; nurse and enthusiastic candidate. Not endorsed.
Editorial endorses Sarah J. Beale for school board District 5. Led primary voting overwhelmingly; teaches high school dropouts at Guilford Technical Institute.
Editorial endorses Sylvia Berkelhammer for school board District 6 (northwest). Former school teacher; master's in education from UNC-G.
District 6 opponent; second VP and associate actuary at Jefferson Standard; past co-president of Bluford PTA. Editorial says 'either nominee would serve well' but prefers Berkelhammer. Not endorsed.
At-large opponent for Greensboro school board. Long career in public education, vice-chairman of Parents Council on Education. Not endorsed.

Editorial 'For city school board' endorses J.E. 'Eddie' Hicks for at-large seat on Greensboro city school board. Businessman with knowledge of budget affairs and business management; Claxton PTA president and VP of Chamber of Commerce.

Editorial endorses Republican Dorothy Burnley of High Point for State House. Combines fiscal restraint with social concern; former president of High Point Women's Shelter; longtime civic and party activist.
Editorial endorses Republican incumbent J. Howard Coble for State House. Greensboro lawyer; served in Holshouser administration; gets along with colleagues and is effective.
Editorial endorses Democrat Ralph Edwards for State House. Savings and loan official; won primary ticket this spring; long active in local civic affairs.

Editorial endorses incumbent Democrat Byron Haworth for second consecutive term in State House. Retired district court judge; conscientious in legislative duties; special interest in legislation affecting elderly.

Editorial endorses Republican incumbent Margaret Keesee for State House. Greensboro kindergarten teacher; combines fiscal conservatism with activist approach to social issues; education her top priority.
Editorial '...And in the House' endorses incumbent Democrat Jim Morgan (High Point attorney, chairman of delegation) for NC State House. 'One of the ablest young legislators in the state.'
Editorial endorses incumbent Democrat Mary Seymour for third term in State House. Former mayor pro tem of Greensboro; effective in lobbying for local needs.
Republican incumbent State Senator. Greensboro businessman; editorial criticizes him for 'narrow, obstructionist approach' and political excesses including a botched ERA poll. Not endorsed.
Republican State Senate candidate; insurance company manager; ran and lost in 1978. Editorial says he 'impressed us with his thoughtful attention to issues' but did not endorse.
Editorial endorses Democrat Henry Frye for State Senate. Six terms in House; Greensboro lawyer and banker; respected for principles and pragmatism.
Editorial 'For N.C. Senate' endorses incumbent Democrat Rachel Gray for third term in NC State Senate. Former mayor pro tem of High Point; led ticket in 1978; advocate for equal rights for women.
Editorial endorses Democrat Jim Turner (Greensboro attorney) for State Senate. Narrowly lost in 1978; appointed to fill unexpired term of Sen. Kathy Sebo. 'Highly recommend him.'
Republican State Senate candidate; Quaker minister, newcomer to politics. 'Lacks the season of the other candidates.' Not endorsed.
